answer.rationale: The write-path p99 degradation began ~30 minutes after the release shipped, making the new build the leading suspect; heavy settlement writes likely amplify a regression the release introduced. Rolling back restores the known-stable prior build and directly protects in-flight customer writes, which fits the objective better than failover (no regional fault signal), capacity (headroom won't fix a code regression), circuit breakers (no partner outage indicated), or read-replica routing (the problem is on the write path, not read load). I verify b1 and b6 to confirm rollback safety and that staged gating makes the prior build trustworthy. If verification contradicted this, I would fall back to add_capacity.
